Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Documented absence of epidemic Vibrio cholerae O1 in Somalia, January 1987 - December 1990, from active laboratory-based diarrhoeal surveillance across numerous Somali regions (Coppo et al., Am J Trop Med Hyg 1995;53(4):351-9, PMID 7485686). Somalia - Somalie 16.III-15.VI .......... 5 826 356 (Notifications received from 28 June to 4 July 1996)' - interpreted as 5826 sCh cases, 356 deaths. Interpreted as 5,826 cholera cases and 356 deaths notified by Somalia for 16 March - 15 June 1996 (CFR 6.1%). This notification period starts the day after the previous one (WER 71(13): '...-15.III', 2,990 cases / 99 deaths, AI row 166), which confirms that the March figure was a cumulative to 15 March and this one is a non-overlapping period increment: 2,990 + 5,826 = 8,816 cases and 455 deaths by mid-June, against JHU's 1996 annual 10,274. CORROBORATION (>1000): the 1996 total is corroborated by JHU/WHO annual (10,274) and the WHO Horn of Africa 2007 profile (~10,000 in 1996, metadata 36); USAID via IRB Canada reports the epidemic 'diminished substantially' about three months after March 1996. Period increment - do not sum with the 1996 cumulative rows (AI 164, 165) except row 166, which it follows; not additive with the JHU 1996 annual. National total - includes provinces not individually listed.

source: WHO Disease Outbreak News: 1997 - Cholera in Somalia - Update (9 May 1997)
processing_notes: Source states: 'A total of 4437 cholera cases with 146 deaths have been reported since the end of November 1997 to 7 May 1997 although the real number of cases is believed to be higher because of the difficulty of data collection. Weekly reports have been made by NGOs working in the country as well as by the local authorities where available.' - interpreted as 4437 sCh cases, 146 deaths. Interpreted as the national cumulative of the 1996-97 epidemic: 4,437 cholera cases and 146 deaths from the end of November 1996 to 7 May 1997. The DON prints 'end of November 1997', an evident typo for 1996 (the period ends 7 May 1997; the preceding DON of 15 April 1997, AI Index 16, counts 1,535 cases / 47 deaths from 30 Nov 1996). WHO adds that the real number is believed higher. CORROBORATION (>1000): JHU/WHO 1997 annual 6,814 / 252 and the earlier DON (Index 16) are consistent. Cumulative - nested with AI Index 16 (to 15 Apr 1997); do not sum. National total - includes provinces not individually listed (the Mogadishu sub-total is a separate row).

processing_notes: Source states: 'A total of over 2 000 cases with 74 deaths has been recorded in the epidemic in Mogadishu but it appears that it has now passed its peak, although high levels are still being reported.' - interpreted as 2000 sCh cases, 74 deaths. source: WHO Disease Outbreak News: 1999 - Cholera in Somalia - Update 2 (8 September 1999)
processing_notes: Source states: 'The disease is appearing in new areas and since 1 August, 3-4 cases of watery diarrhoea have been registered every day at Bosaso hospital; in all 190 cases have been admitted, of which 84 were males and 106 females (F:M ratio, 1.26:1).
